panels.description: Warm evening exterior of an ordinary, well-kept 2070 house on a quiet street. Integrated solar roof tiles catch honey-colored light, a maintained vegetable garden borders the walk, and an ordinary ten-year-old car sits in the drive. Comfortable and lived-in, never flashy; no extra futuristic infrastructure or readable signage.

Human-scale interior hallway in the same home, with a dense but orderly wall of framed patents, machine photographs, news clippings and photographs. Alex stands beside the wall; Alex is a man in his mid-40s in the 2070 scenes, of average height with a lean, capable repairer's build, squared shoulders and work-worn hands; he has a long, calm face, grey at the temples, close-cropped dark hair, medium-brown skin and steady dark eyes, and wears a plain charcoal-brown sweater over a pale shirt with practical dark trousers. His left wrist is partly hidden beneath his sleeve. His approximately nine-year-old daughter stands on tiptoe, studying the objects one by one. Keep the upper area above the figures and wall clear for later lettering.

Close enough for a wall cluster to read without becoming an infographic: make the two framed headlines readable, along with a photograph of separate founders beside separate water units and different shop signs. Include patent diagrams, machine photographs and the framed photograph of four unnamed collaborators laughing together in a lab. Keep the frames orderly but varied in age; reserve clean negative space above the cluster for lettering.

The daughter points into the wall between the patent records and machine photographs, then looks back toward Alex. Her body is short and slight, with a child's soft, round face, warm-brown skin, large dark eyes and thick dark hair gathered into two low, slightly uneven braids; she wears a mustard-yellow cardigan over a pale blue school shirt, a knee-length navy skirt, white socks and scuffed red sneakers. She rises onto her toes, head tilted forward with direct curiosity. Keep the upper-right area open for her balloon.
